note: Fixed sentences of the comparison email. Written from the old skill's rules in plain English (04/11/2026); the program fills the {fields}. Paul may change any of them here, in Claude Code.
intro1: This table puts the main features of each plan side by side, so you can see at a glance how the offers differ. It also shows the once-off costs you pay when the plan starts.
intro2: This is the real yearly cost of each plan, split into its separate fees. We show the fees one by one because a single combined figure (the Effective Annual Cost, or EAC: one blended percentage that mixes several different fees together) hides which fee is driving the cost. These percentages are charged each year on the value of your fund.
intro3: This table shows what each fund aims to do and how it has performed over 1, 3 and 5 years (per year), taken from the fund's own fact sheet and dated as shown. Past performance is useful background, but it does not guarantee future returns and it is not the reason to choose a plan.
intro4: Some plans add a loyalty bonus or reward. These are a small extra, not the main reason to choose a plan, so we keep them short.
things_heading: Things to know before you read the tables:
tk_mismatch: The quotes are not for the same {field}: {detail}. They are shown as quoted, so this is not a like-for-like comparison.
tk_stale: The fact sheet for the {fund} is dated {date}, which is more than three months ago, so its figures may be out of date.
tk_notfound: A current fact sheet for the {fund} could not be found, so its performance is not shown.
tk_supplement: {provider}'s {doc} (dated {date}) shows {field} as {supplement_value}, but the formal quote shows {quote_value}. Please confirm with {provider} which figure applies before relying on the {doc}.
perf_fee_note: Performance fee: the {fund} can charge a performance fee ({note}). It is not included in the total above because it varies from year to year.
tax_ra_intro: This explains how tax works for the plans above.
tax_ra: Contributions to a retirement annuity are tax deductible up to 27,5% of your remuneration, capped at the SARS annual limit. This is the same by law for every provider, so no plan is more tax efficient than another.
tax_tfsa: SARS allows you to contribute up to {annual} a year and {lifetime} over your lifetime to a tax-free savings account. You have already contributed {annual_used} this tax year and {lifetime_used} in total, so you have {annual_left} left this tax year and {lifetime_left} left for life.
tax_tfsa_over: This would take you over your {which} limit by {excess}.
flex_intro: This shows how free you are to change the plan later.
verdict_heading: Fees only: how the plans compare
verdict_intro: This looks at one thing only, the yearly cost of each plan from the fee table above. It is not advice on which fund will perform better.
verdict_summary: {cheapest} has the lowest total ongoing fees: {diff} percentage points a year less than {next}.
verdict_example: As an example only, on a fund value of {value}, that difference is about {rand} a year.
